quandoUsar: A problem the user must resolve to continue, such as a declined payment or nearly full storage, shown where it happens.
A message that changes state in place, such as a check that goes from `info` to `success`: the icon morphs and the height follows the new text with a spring.
Notices the user can dismiss (`onDismiss`): when it goes away, the alert collapses its height and the content below moves up without jumping.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast` to confirm an action completed in the background that asks nothing of the user.
Use `announcement-bar` for a site-wide message at the top of the page, such as a promotion or a launch.
Use `dialog` when the user must decide something before continuing.
acessibilidade: The `danger` tone uses `role="alert"`, which interrupts the screen reader; the other tones use `role="status"`, which is read without interrupting. Reserve `danger` for what is urgent.
The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so the title must say what happened; when the title or text changes, the outgoing copy is hidden and only the current text is read.
The close button is a native `<button>` with a fixed English `aria-label` (`Dismiss: <título>`); on a non-English site, adjust that text in the copied file.
movimento: Changing `tone` morphs the icon in place (the old one shrinks with a slight blur and the new one grows), and a new title or text rises while the previous one exits upward.
The text column animates its height with a no-overshoot spring right after a content change; passive changes, such as resizing the window, follow immediately.
With `open` or `onDismiss`, appearing and disappearing collapse the height along with the fade; with “reduce motion”, the text only fades, and height, entrance, and exit change without animation.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/alert/alert`; `title` is required and the children become the description. Without `open` and without `onDismiss`, the alert appears without an entrance animation (tone and text changes still animate).
Controlled: pass `open` and, in `onDismiss`, set `open` to `false`. Without `open`, the alert collapses itself on close and only then calls `onDismiss`.
Choose `tone` by its effect: `danger` only for a blocking error, because it is announced immediately; `warning` for imminent risk; `success` and `info` for the rest.

quandoUsar: A site-wide message at the top of the page: a time-limited promotion, a new version, or a live event, with an action link.
Two to four messages that rotate in the same space, pausing on hover or focus and, with `controls`, previous, next, and pause buttons.
Campaigns the user closes once: with `id`, the dismissal is saved in `localStorage` and the bar does not come back; change the `id` to show a new campaign to everyone.
quandoEvitar: Use `alert` for a message tied to a specific screen or form, helping to resolve a problem there.
Use `toast` or `toast-stack` for the result of something the user just did.
Use `countdown` when the countdown is the centerpiece of the page, such as a launch screen, and not a detail in a strip.

teclado.acao: Moves through the action link and the previous, pause, next, and close buttons; while focus is inside the bar, rotation stays paused.

acessibilidade: It is a `<section>` with `aria-label` (default “Announcements”); with more than one message it becomes a carousel (`aria-roledescription`) and each message is a labeled group “N of M”.
While it rotates on its own, the messages area has `aria-live="off"` so it does not speak on every change; when stopped by pause, focus, mouse, or “reduce motion”, it switches to `polite`.
The button labels (“Previous announcement”, “Pause announcements”, “Dismiss”) and the countdown reading are fixed in English; pass `label` in your language and adjust the rest in the copied file.
movimento: The next message rises from below with a slight blur while the previous one exits upward (going back reverses the path), and the bar follows the new message's height with a no-overshoot spring.

The pause ring is the rotation clock: it fills linearly during `interval`, stops where it is when paused, and completes the rest on resume; in the countdown, each digit that changes drops in from above.
Closing collapses the height with a spring and the page moves up with it. With “reduce motion”, automatic rotation is turned off, messages only fade, and closing becomes a short fade.
responsivo: Below 560 px of the bar's own width (container query), the column that mirrors the buttons disappears and the message aligns left instead of centering.
Message, countdown, and link wrap onto lines when space runs out (the countdown and the link do not break internally), and the bar grows to the new height with the spring.
desempenho: Each countdown wakes once per second, aligned to the full second; the rotation is a linear animation that stops when the tab is hidden, the mouse is over it, or focus is inside.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/announcement-bar/announcement-bar`; each item in `messages` needs a stable `id`. The bar stays in the flow (it is not fixed or sticky): place it above the header.

With controlled `open`, the dismissal is written to `localStorage` (when there is an `id`) but not read; to remember it, keep the state in the component. `clearAnnouncementDismissal(id)` erases the dismissal, and the bar returns on the next mount.

`controls` is off by default (only the close button appears). `countdown.to` goes through `new Date()`; use an ISO date with a time zone (`Z` or `-03:00`) so it does not depend on the visitor's time zone.

quandoUsar: Ask for consent to optional cookies on the first visit, with accept, reject, and customize side by side, and declining as easy as accepting.
Let the user change their mind later: the choice becomes a round button in the corner that reopens the preferences, and `openPreferences()` through the `ref` serves a “Cookies” link in the footer.
Ask again when the policy changes: increase `version` and the choice saved under `storageKey` stops being valid.
quandoEvitar: Use `announcement-bar` for a top message that asks for no choice.
Use `dialog` when the flow requires blocking the page until a decision is made; this layer is not modal and the site remains usable behind it.
Use `switch` directly on a settings page when the privacy preferences are part of a larger form.

teclado.acao: With focus in the preferences panel, closes without saving and returns focus to the bar's “Customize” button or to the reopen button.
On a category's switch, toggles it in the draft; nothing is saved until “Save choices”, “Accept all”, or “Reject all”.
Moves through buttons and switches; there is no focus trap, because the layer is not modal.

acessibilidade: Bar and panel are `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="false"`, with no focus trap; opening the panel moves focus to the title, and saving or closing returns focus to the bar or to the reopen button.
Each switch has a `<label>` and `aria-describedby` with the category description, and “Save choices” reports in hidden text how many optional categories are allowed.
The default texts are in English; pass `labels` (message, buttons, title, `reopen`, `alwaysOn`, `close`) to translate them, including the accessible names of the reopen and close buttons.
movimento: A single surface changes position, width, height, and radius with a no-overshoot spring between bar, panel, and round button; growing is slightly slower than shrinking.
The content of each shape swaps with a short fade, rising a few pixels from a slight blur, and the surface enters from below at nearly full scale.
With “reduce motion”, the shape changes immediately and only the content fades.
responsivo: The bar goes up to 660 px and the panel up to 420 px; below 560 px the bar stacks text and buttons, and in a very narrow bar (around 340 px) “Customize” drops to its own line.
The category list scrolls internally above `min(46vh, 300px)`; change the limit with the `--cookie-consent-list-max` variable.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/cookie-consent/cookie-consent` (it uses `button` and `switch`). It only records the choice: load analytics or marketing scripts yourself, from `onChange` or `readCookieConsent(storageKey, version)`.
Mount it once in the layout with `storageKey`; nothing appears on the server or before storage is read. In a preview inside a card, use `strategy="absolute"` with a positioned parent.
For a “Cookies” link in the footer, keep a `ref` and call `openPreferences()`; `reset()` erases the choice and shows the bar again.

quandoUsar: A fixed moment people are waiting for, such as a launch, a live event, or a registration deadline, with large digits in the center of a section (`variant="large"`).
A deadline inside a banner, card, or table cell, on a single line (`variant="compact"`).
Screens that must change on their own at zero: the digits become `completeLabel` (default “Live now”) and `onComplete` fires once, immediately, even with the tab hidden.
quandoEvitar: It does not suit elapsed time, such as a stopwatch counting up: it only counts down to `target`.
Use `announcement-bar` when the deadline accompanies a message at the top of the site; it has its own countdown inside the message.
Use `slot-text` or `animated-counter` for numbers that change by event, such as a price or total, with no clock behind them.
acessibilidade: The root is `role="timer"` named by `label` (default “Time remaining”); the animated digits are hidden and a hidden text states the time in full, without seconds while more than a minute remains.
`role="timer"` does not announce changes; if the end matters to screen reader users, announce it in your own live region from `onComplete`.
The unit names, both visible and read aloud (“Days”, “3 days, 4 hours”), are in English; pass `label` in your language and translate the units in the copied file.
movimento: Each digit is a wheel that turns by the shortest path, downward each second (00 → 59 is a single step); on first display, the wheels enter in sequence, left to right.
At zero, the digits dissolve with slight scale and blur and give way to `completeLabel`, and the box follows the new width and height with a spring; in `compact`, the pill takes on the success tone.
With “reduce motion”, the digits change without turning, the final swap is a short fade, and the pulsing dot next to the label stays still.
responsivo: In `large`, the digit size follows the container width (`cqi` unit), from 1.75 rem up to display size, and four groups fit in 320 px.
desempenho: The clock only advances while the component is on screen and the tab is visible, and on return it rereads the time, without accumulating delay; a separate timer guarantees the end on time.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/countdown/countdown`. For a local time, pass `target="2026-12-01T10:00"` and `timeZone="America/Sao_Paulo"`; a string without a time zone and without `timeZone` is read as UTC.
`units` defines what appears, and the largest unit absorbs the rest: with `["hours", "minutes"]`, hours go past 24. If the device clock is not reliable, pass `clock` with the server time.
`onComplete` only fires if the count reaches zero while the component is mounted; if `target` has already passed on mount, it shows `completeLabel` without counting and without calling the callback.

quandoUsar: A short wait with no known progress, such as opening an invoice, submitting a form, or fetching results.
Inside a button or a sentence, with `size="sm"` and `tone="current"` to inherit the text color.
Waits with their own meaning: `dots` for “someone is typing”, `bars` for audio loading, `ring` for waiting on a live signal, and `orbit` for longer tasks.
quandoEvitar: Use `progress` when you know how much remains: a bar with a number says more than an endless spin.
Use `skeleton` when the wait is for the content of an area whose shape you already know.
Use `loading-states` or `text-shimmer` for the “thinking” state of AI interfaces, with status text.
acessibilidade: The root is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, and `label` (default “Loading”) is the text that is read; the drawing is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
Write in `label` what is loading (“Saving changes”), not just “Loading”; `showLabel` shows the same text next to the drawing.
Each loader is a live region: avoid several on screen at once and, inside a button, mark the button with `aria-busy`, as in the demo.
movimento: Everything is a looping CSS animation: the `spinner` arc stretches and shrinks as it turns, the dots make a wave, the bars pulse like an equalizer, the ring emits two waves, and three satellites orbit together.
`speed` multiplies the pace of any variant: 2 is double speed and 0.5 is half.
With “reduce motion”, nothing moves: each variant stops in a readable shape and the whole drawing only pulses its opacity slowly, so it still says “working”.
desempenho: The animation is CSS only (keyframes), with no timers or React re-renders, so several loaders on the page cost no JavaScript.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/loader/loader`. The props that matter are `variant`, `size` (`sm` 16 px, `md` 24 px, `lg` 40 px), and `label`; the square is the same in every variant, so switching does not shift the layout.
Inside a button, use `size="sm"` and `tone="current"` to inherit the text color; the default `accent` paints with the accent color.
There is no delay or visibility prop: render the loader only during the wait and remove it when the wait ends.

quandoUsar: The initial setup of an account or workspace, with three to eight steps that can be done in any order.
Steps the interface itself performs: with `actionLabel` and an asynchronous `onAction`, the button shows loading, marks the step when done, and shows the error message if it fails.
A welcome card the user can collapse (`defaultHidden`, `onHiddenChange`) and which, at the end, swaps `title` for `doneTitle`.
quandoEvitar: Use `stepper` when the order is mandatory, such as in a checkout where one step unlocks the next.
Use `todo-list` to show an AI agent's plan advancing on its own, with the user checking nothing.
Use `checkbox` for a simple task list, with no details or per-item actions.

teclado.acao: With focus on a step's title, moves to the previous or next title, wrapping around at the end of the list.
Moves to the title of the first or last step in the list.
On the title, opens or closes the step's details; on the circle, checks or unchecks; on the action, runs `onAction`.

acessibilidade: Each circle is a button with `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked`, named by the step's title; the title opens the details with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
The ring is `role="progressbar"` (“N of M steps done”) and a `role="status"` region announces each step done or undone; the `onAction` error appears with `role="alert"`.
When a focused step collapses, focus moves to the action of the next open step, and unchecking in the completed group moves focus to the circle of the step that came back.
movimento: On checking, the circle fills from the center and the checkmark draws itself; the title gets a strikethrough that crosses the line and, after 0.72 s, the step collapses into the completed group.

Rows and panels open and close their height with a no-overshoot spring; the ring fills with each step, the numbers turn in the direction of the change, and a checkmark appears in the ring when everything is finished.
With “reduce motion”, heights change immediately with a short fade, strikethrough and fill appear without transition, and the action button's spinner stops.
responsivo: In a card narrower than 380 px (container query), the hide button shows only the arrow and keeps its spoken name.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/onboarding-checklist/onboarding-checklist`. It is uncontrolled: pass `defaultCompleted` with the ids already done and save progress from `onCompletedChange`.
In `onAction`, return a Promise: resolving marks the step; throwing `new Error("mensagem")` keeps the step open with the message. Without `actionLabel`, the step is only checked by hand.
The fixed texts (“Setup progress”, “Hide”, “completed”, the default error message) are in English; translate them in the copied file. Each step needs a stable `id`.

quandoUsar: A task with a known end, such as a file upload, an import, or multi-stage processing, with the number alongside (`showValue`).
Fill measures that are not time, such as a profile 72% complete or 18 of 50 GB used (`value` and `max`).
When the end deserves a signal: at 100% the bar takes on the success color and a checkmark appears next to the number.
quandoEvitar: Use `loader` when there is no way to know how much remains; this bar has no indeterminate mode.
Use `usage-meter` for a quota split by category, with a limit and a nearly-full warning.
Use `toast-progress` to track a background task without taking up space on the page.
acessibilidade: It is `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` as a percentage; the name comes from `label` and, without it, is the generic “Progress”.
Always pass `label` saying what is advancing (“Uploading report.pdf”): it is the accessible name and also the visible text above the bar.
movimento: A single no-overshoot spring moves the fill and counts the number, so the two always match; the fill slides in from the left instead of stretching, and the rounded tip keeps its shape.
On reaching 100%, the checkmark enters with a small delay next to the number and the color changes to the success one; changing `label` makes the new text rise with a slight blur.
With “reduce motion”, the bar jumps to the value, the label only fades, and the color changes without transition.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/progress/progress`. `value` goes from 0 to `max` (default 100) and is clamped to that range; there is no indeterminate mode.
It fills the parent's full width, so give the container a width. Update `value` freely: each change only redirects the spring.
With `max`, the displayed number remains a percentage (18 of 50 becomes 36%); if you want “18 of 50 GB”, write that in `label`.

quandoUsar: Lists where pulling down is the expected gesture on mobile, such as an inbox, a feed, or notifications.
An area with its own scrolling inside a panel or an app frame (`height`), which refreshes the content without reloading the page.
Updates that sometimes start outside the gesture, from a button or a timer: `refreshing` shows the same refresh state.
quandoEvitar: It does not suit a whole page scrolling on the `body`: the gesture only exists inside its own container, which needs a height.
Use `infinite-masonry` when new content should arrive on scrolling to the end, not on pulling the top.
Use `message-scroller` for conversations, where new content arrives at the end of the list.

teclado.acao: The component's first focus stop is the `refreshLabel` button (default “Refresh”), which only appears with keyboard focus; the next `Tab` goes to the scroll area.
On the button, triggers the same `onRefresh` as the gesture; during the refresh it is `aria-disabled` and does not repeat.
With focus on the scroll area, scroll the content (native behavior).

acessibilidade: The scroll area is `role="region"`, focusable, with `aria-busy` during the refresh; replace the generic name from `label` (default “Content”) with the name of the list.
A `role="status"` region announces “Refreshing” and “Updated” (fixed in English in the code), and the visual indicator is `aria-hidden`.
movimento: The content follows the finger 1:1 at the start and with increasing resistance up to `maxPull`; the indicator appears, grows, the arrow flips and, past `threshold`, it stretches into a capsule in the accent color.
On release past the limit, the content holds at up to 56 px while the indicator spins; when the Promise finishes, a checkmark appears for 0.65 s and everything returns with a no-overshoot spring.
With “reduce motion”, the returns become jumps, the icons only fade, and the spin slows down (2.4 s per turn).
responsivo: It fills the parent's height by default; if the parent has no defined height, pass `height` so the area can scroll.
`overscroll-behavior` prevents the pull from passing to the page and triggering the browser's own reload on mobile.
desempenho: The pull animates a single motion value (transform), with no React re-render on every frame; touch uses a non-passive listener so it can block scrolling only during the gesture.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/pull-to-refresh/pull-to-refresh`. `onRefresh` should return a Promise: the indicator spins until it finishes; without a Promise, it spins for 0.6 s.
Give the component a height (`height` or a parent with a height) and put the list inside it: it is itself the scrolling area.
On desktop, dragging with the mouse is not obvious; also keep a visible button that calls the same function and show the state with `refreshing`.

quandoUsar: Reserve the space of a comment, card, or block of text while the data arrives, so the page does not jump when it appears.
Swap the placeholder for the real content in the same place: with children and `loading`, the skeleton fades into the content and the height follows with a spring.
List items with a photo and text, such as comments or contacts (`avatar` and `lines`).
quandoEvitar: Use `loader` for a short action, such as saving, where there is no block of content to reserve.
Use `progress` when the wait has a known end and it is worth showing how much remains.
For tables, charts, or layouts that do not look like lines of text, draw a custom skeleton: this one only makes an avatar and up to six lines.
acessibilidade: The placeholder is `role="status"` with `aria-busy` and the name from `label` (default “Loading content”, in English); the blocks are `aria-hidden`. Say in `label` what is loading.
With children, the container has `aria-busy` while `loading` is `true`, and the content only enters the DOM when the wait ends.
movimento: The blocks pulse their opacity in a wave, each one a little after the one above, and stop after about 20 s so they do not pulse forever.
When `loading` becomes `false`, the skeleton fades, the content enters rising 4 px, and the height goes from the skeleton's size to the content's with a no-overshoot spring.
With “reduce motion”, the pulse is turned off and the swap becomes a short fade, without animating the height.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/skeleton/skeleton`. Two uses: standalone, as a placeholder, or wrapping the real content with `loading={isLoading}`, which handles the swap and the height.
`lines` goes from 1 to 6 and `avatar` adds a circle on the left; choose a number of lines similar to the final content so the height changes little.
`loading` only has an effect with children; without children, the component always shows the skeleton, so render it only during the wait.

quandoUsar: Show which step of a checkout, sign-up, or setup the user is on, above the content (`horizontal`) or beside it (`vertical`).
Flows where it is possible to go back to a step already done: with `onStepSelect`, completed steps become buttons.
Flag a step that failed, such as a declined card: `error` swaps the number for an alert and the message takes the place of the description.
quandoEvitar: Use `onboarding-checklist` when the steps can be done in any order and checked by hand.
Use `tabs` when the sections are independent and the user can move back and forth between them freely.
Use `adaptive-stepper` to choose a number with minus and plus buttons; despite the similar name, this item indicates steps.

teclado.acao: With `onStepSelect`, move focus between the completed steps and the current one, without wrapping; in right-to-left text, ← and → are swapped.
Moves to the first step or to the current step.
On a completed step, calls `onStepSelect` with its index.

acessibilidade: Without `onStepSelect` it is a read-only `role="group"`; with it, it becomes a `<nav>` of buttons. The current step has `aria-current="step"` and each step has its state in hidden text (“Completed”, “Error”).
An `aria-live="polite"` region announces “Step N of M: label” on each change of `current`, and `completeLabel` at the end; these fixed texts are in English.
Only completed steps enter the `Tab` order; the current and future ones have `aria-disabled`, and the arrow keys also reach the current one.
movimento: On advancing, the line between steps fills with a spring starting from the step that finished; skipping several steps fills one line after another, and the current step's ring appears last.
A completed step's number shrinks and gives way to a drawn checkmark (on an error, an exclamation mark); new descriptions rise with a slight blur and the height follows.
With “reduce motion”, lines, markers, and texts change immediately.
responsivo: The horizontal one measures its own width (container query): below 30 rem it hides the labels, keeps the markers, and shows the current step's label and description underneath; `compact` forces this mode.
With `details="current"`, only the current step shows its description, which saves height; errors always appear.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/stepper/stepper`. It is controlled by `current`, the index of the step in progress; use `current={steps.length}` to mark the whole flow as completed.
The stepper only indicates: each step's content and the back and continue buttons are up to you, by changing `current`.
To go back to completed steps, pass `onStepSelect={setCurrent}`; only indices lower than `current` fire. The error goes on the step itself, in `steps[i].error`.

quandoUsar: Confirm an action that succeeded and asks nothing more: draft saved, link copied, invitation sent.
A single notice at a time, in a place you control, with `open` and `onOpenChange` tied to the screen's state.
Touch screens where swiping the notice sideways is the natural way to dismiss it.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast-action` when the notice offers undo or another action; its timer pauses on mouse and focus.
Use `toast-stack` for several notices in a row or of different types (error, warning, loading); this one only shows the success checkmark.
Use `alert` for errors and warnings that must stay on screen until the user acts.
acessibilidade: It is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic`: the screen reader reads title and description together, without interrupting, and the outgoing copies are hidden.
The timer does not pause on mouse or focus and there is no shortcut to reach the notice; do not put anything in it that the user needs to read carefully or act on.
The close button is a `<button>` with `aria-label` “Dismiss notification”, fixed in English in the file.
movimento: It enters rising 16 px from a slightly smaller scale, with a no-overshoot spring, while the checkmark draws itself; on closing, it drops a little and fades.
When dragged sideways, it follows the finger; past 80 px or released quickly, it flies off in the direction of the gesture at the release velocity, otherwise it springs back.
With “reduce motion”, entrance and exit become a short fade and dragging is turned off.
responsivo: The width goes up to 26 rem and fits the parent; the title stays on one line and is truncated with an ellipsis, so put long details in `description`, which wraps.
notasIA: Import the default: `import Toast from "@/components/ryan-ui/toast/toast"` (there is no named export). It appears where it is rendered; position it yourself, for example in a fixed container in the corner.

Automatic closing (`duration`, default 4500 ms) only works with `onOpenChange`; pass a stable function, such as the `setOpen` from `useState`, because a new function on every render restarts the countdown.
To show the notice again, set `open` back to `true`; changing `title` while it is open swaps the text in place, without restarting the timer.

quandoUsar: Right after something reversible, such as deleting, archiving, or sending, offering “Undo” while the timer bar runs.
When the user needs time to react: the countdown stops with the mouse over it, with focus, or with the tab hidden and resumes where it left off.
When the result of the action should be clear: on tapping it, the text swaps to `confirmation` with a drawn checkmark before the notice leaves.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast` for a simple confirmation, with no action.
Use `toast-stack` when several notices may arrive in sequence; this one shows one at a time.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` when the destructive action should be confirmed beforehand, not undone afterward.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the open notice's action (or to the close button, after the action), to reach it before the time runs out; turn off with `hotkey={false}`.
With focus inside the notice, the countdown pauses; on leaving, it resumes where it left off.
On the action, runs `onAction` and shows the confirmation; focus moves to the close button.
With focus inside, closes the notice and returns focus to where it was before.

acessibilidade: It is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`; the outgoing copy is hidden, so only the current text is read, including the confirmation.
On closing with focus inside, it returns to where it was before entering the notice; after the action, it goes to the close button instead of dropping onto the page.
`duration={0}` keeps the notice until it is closed, for those who need more time; the close `aria-label` is fixed in English (“Dismiss notification”).
movimento: A thin bar at the bottom empties at a linear pace until the notice leaves; while the countdown is paused, it appears dimmer.
On taking the action, the icon shrinks with blur and a checkmark draws itself in its place, the text swaps rising and the height follows with a spring; the action button leaves the flow and fades.
It enters rising with a spring and flies off when dragged sideways. With “reduce motion”, the bar drops in 8 steps, everything only fades, and dragging is turned off.
responsivo: In `bottom-*` positions it is fixed to the window at up to 24 rem and, on screens below 30 rem, centers at the bottom; with `contained`, it attaches to the positioned ancestor.
In a notice narrower than 23 rem, the action drops below the text instead of squeezing it.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/toast-action/toast-action`. Undo the operation in `onAction` and only delete for good in `onOpenChange` when the reason is not `"action"`.
To repeat the notice on an identical event (the same file deleted twice), change `resetKey`: the action comes back and the bar fills again.
Use `position="bottom-center"` (or another corner) to fix it to the window, or `inline` to stay in the flow; in a preview inside a panel, add `contained` and give the parent `position: relative`.

quandoUsar: Track a background task with a known percentage, such as an upload, export, or import, without blocking the screen.
Close the loop in the same notice: the bar completes and becomes a success checkmark, or freezes in the danger tone with “Retry” on failure.
Progress with a detail that changes on each update (“27 of 42 MB”, “3 seconds left”) in `description`, without animating the text swap every time.
quandoEvitar: Use `progress` when the progress should be visible on the page itself, near what is being processed.
Use `toast-stack` with `update` for several tasks at once; this one tracks only one.
Use `toast` for a result that needed no progress.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to “Retry”, when the task failed, or to the close button; turn off with `hotkey={false}`.
With focus inside, closes the notice (reason `dismiss`) and returns focus to where it was.
On “Retry”, calls `onRetry`; focus moves to the close button while the task restarts.

acessibilidade: The notice is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, and the bar is `role="progressbar"` named by the title, with `aria-valuetext` coming from `formatValue`.
While the task runs, the description that changes on each update has `aria-live="off"` and the number next to the title is `aria-hidden`, so there is no reading at every step.
On closing with focus inside, it returns to where it was; the close `aria-label` is fixed in English (“Dismiss notification”).
movimento: Bar and number slide together to each new `value` with a spring; at the end, the bar completes in 0.32 s and only then does the notice change to success.

On the state change, the spinner shrinks with blur and a checkmark or an exclamation mark draws itself; the text swaps rising, the number gives way to “Retry” and, on success, the bar thins and disappears.
With “reduce motion”, the bar jumps to the value, the spinner stays still, swaps only fade, and drag-to-dismiss is turned off.
responsivo: In `bottom-*` positions it is fixed to the window at up to 24 rem and centers at the bottom below 30 rem; with `contained`, it attaches to the positioned ancestor.
In a narrow notice (under 23 rem), “Retry” drops below the text.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/toast-progress/toast-progress`. Update `value`; without `status`, reaching 100 already shows success. Failure needs `status="error"`, and to resume go back to `"loading"`.

Pass the current state's text in `title`. While running or in error, the notice does not close on its own; success closes after `duration`, which restarts from zero if the user holds the notice with the mouse or focus.
Without `onRetry`, the error appears without a button. If another notice on the page also uses `Alt + T` (`toast-stack`, `toast-action`), turn off `hotkey` on one of them.

quandoUsar: Short results of several actions in sequence, such as save, delete, and sync, stacked in a corner without covering the screen.
Notices that change in place: a `loading` that becomes `success` with `update(id, …)`, or an “Undo” that becomes “Restored”.
Notices of different types in the same place (`success`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, `loading`), with a longer duration for warnings and errors.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast` or `toast-action` when only one notice appears at a time and you want to control `open` directly on the component.
Use `notification-center` for a history the user consults later, with read and unread.
Use `alert` for errors that must stay visible until they are resolved.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the first button of the front notice and opens the stack as a list; turn off with `hotkey={false}`.
Moves through actions and close buttons; with keyboard focus inside, the stack stays open and the timers pause.
Closes the focused notice; focus moves to the next notice or returns to where it was before.
On the action, runs `onClick`; the notice closes, unless the handler updates it.

acessibilidade: The stack is a `<section>` with `aria-live="polite"` that announces new notices and text changes; each notice starts with its type in hidden text (“Success:”, “Error:”), in English.
The region's name includes the shortcut (“Notifications (Alt+T)”), and notices beyond `visibleToasts` stay `inert` until they reach the front.
When an action updates the notice and it goes away, keyboard focus moves to the close button; on closing, it moves on to the next notice or returns to where it was.
movimento: New notices rise from the edge and earlier ones stay behind, 14 px higher and slightly smaller; hovering or focusing opens the stack into a list, with a no-overshoot spring.
Dragged to the right, the notice follows the finger and flies off when it passes 40% of the width, counting momentum; to the left, it resists as at the end of a scroll.
`update` swaps icon, text, and height in place and restarts the timer. With “reduce motion”, positions and sizes change immediately and only opacity animates.
responsivo: The stack is up to 22.5 rem wide and fixed in the chosen corner; on screens below 30 rem it centers at the bottom. On touch, which has no hover, tapping a notice opens or closes the stack.
In a notice narrower than 21 rem, the action drops below the text.
desempenho: The stack's geometry lives in motion values, so following the finger, the mouse, or a timer does not re-render React on every frame; the queue holds at most `limit` notices (default 12).
notasIA: Import `ToastStackProvider`, `useToastStack`, and the default `ToastStack` from `@/components/ryan-ui/toast-stack/toast-stack`; wrap the app in the provider, render `<ToastStack />` once, and call `toast()` below it.
`toast()` returns the id: keep it for `update(id, { type: "success", … })` or `dismiss(id)`. Repeating an `id` in `toast()` updates instead of stacking.
`loading` notices do not close on their own, so always update or dismiss them later. In a preview, use `contained` inside a parent with `position: relative`.

quandoUsar: A fixed plan quota, such as storage, seats, or credits, when it matters to see what takes up the space and how much remains until the limit.
Warn before the limit: from `warnAt` (default 90%) the badge shows “Almost full”, and above the limit the excess portion appears hatched, with a marker at the limit.
Plan and billing screens where the user explores the categories by hovering, tapping, or using the arrow keys in the legend.
quandoEvitar: Use `progress` for a single progress measure, without categories or a plan limit.
Use `composition-chart` or `donut-chart` for the breakdown of a whole with no limit, or with more than four parts.
Use `gauge` for a single value within a known range.

teclado.acao: The legend is a single `Tab` stop (roving tabindex); focus already highlights the category in the bar and in the big number.
Move focus between the categories and the free-space item, wrapping around.
Moves to the first category or to the free-space (or excess) item.
Pins the highlight on the focused category (`aria-pressed`); again, unpins.
Unpins the pinned category.

acessibilidade: The bar is `role="img"` with a full summary in `aria-label` (total, each category, and free space); the spinning numbers are `aria-hidden` and there is a hidden text with the total.
The legend is a group of buttons with roving tabindex and `aria-pressed`; a live region only speaks when the state changes (normal, almost full, over the limit) or the excess changes.
Above the limit, the excess is hatched as well as colored and the badge gains an icon, so the state does not depend on color alone.
movimento: The first time it appears on screen, the segments grow from left to right, one after another; afterward, each change makes them all slide with a no-overshoot spring.
The numbers spin like an odometer in the direction of the change, the badge adjusts its width with a spring, and highlighting a category dims the others.
With “reduce motion”, values and widths change immediately and the texts only fade.
responsivo: The legend is an `auto-fit` grid with columns of at least 108 px, which becomes more rows in a narrow card; a long title wraps next to the badge.
desempenho: It waits for 40% of the meter to enter the screen before animating and watches the bar's width with a `ResizeObserver`; the segment positions come from motion values, with no per-frame re-render.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/usage-meter/usage-meter`. Pass `segments` with a stable `id` (changing the value keeps the segment and animates), `limit` in the same unit, and `unit`, such as `"GB"`.
Use at most four segments: the CSS only defines colors for four, and a fifth has no color in the bar and the legend.

Numbers come out in en-US format (decimal point) and the texts (“of 50 GB used”, “Almost full”) are in English; `freeLabel` and `overLabel` translate only part, the rest is adjusted in the copied file.

quandoUsar: Section titles on long pages, such as landing pages and product pages, that enter when the section reaches the screen.
Different entrance tones: `blur` suits almost any title, `word` and `line` suit editorial pages, `tracking` suits short highlight titles, and `wipe` reveals from left to right.
Titles with hand-picked line breaks, by passing `lines` in the `line` variant.
quandoEvitar: Use `text-reveal` for a title that should animate right on mount, such as at the top of the page, without waiting for scroll.
Use `scroll-reveal` to reveal whole blocks on scroll, such as cards, lists, and paragraphs, not just the title.
On work screens the user uses every day, such as dashboards and forms, an animated title only delays reading; use a plain title.
acessibilidade: The title is a real `h2` (or `h1` and `h3` via `as`) with `aria-label` equal to `text`; animated words and letters are `aria-hidden`, so the screen reader reads the whole phrase once.

Titles that are already above the screen are revealed even without passing through it, and on the server a CSS fallback shows the title after 2.4 s if JavaScript is late, so the text is not left hidden.
movimento: `blur` raises each word as it comes out of a blur; `word` and `line` raise words or lines from inside a clip; `tracking` brings the letters closer to normal spacing; `wipe` uncovers the title through a soft edge.
In the per-word variants, the whole sequence lasts at most about 0.4 s; opacity arrives first, blur next, and displacement last, so it is possible to read before it settles.
It fires when 45% of the title is visible; with `once={false}`, it hides again quickly on leaving and animates again on return. With “reduce motion”, it appears finished, without animation.
desempenho: The `tracking` variant creates one element per letter; in long titles, prefer `blur` or `line`.
notasIA: Import `InViewTitle` from `@/components/ryan-ui/in-view-title/in-view-title`; the text goes in `text` (not in children) and the heading level in `as`.
In the `line` variant, pass `lines` with the breaks; without it, the whole title becomes a single line. The other variants break between words.
The animation runs once by default; `once={false}` repeats on every entrance to the screen, and changing the `key` remounts the title and animates again, as in the demo.

quandoUsar: State labels that change a few letters, such as “Publish”, “Publishing”, and “Published”, or “Follow” and “Following”.
Short statuses in buttons, badges, or titles, where the new width should slide instead of jumping and pushing what is beside it.
quandoEvitar: Use `slot-text` for numbers and values that should spin like reels, such as prices and counters.
Use `action-swap` for a compact button that goes through states such as idle, working, and done, with icon and width changing together.
It does not suit long sentences or multi-line text: it stays on a single line and animates letter by letter.
acessibilidade: The current text sits in a visually hidden `span` and the animated letters are `aria-hidden`, so the screen reader reads the whole word, never loose letters.
The swap is not announced; if the change needs to be heard, put the component inside your own `aria-live` region.
movimento: Shared letters slide to the new position with a no-overshoot spring; new ones emerge from a slight blur, in reading order, and removed ones dissolve.
The width follows the new text with the same spring and a soft edge reveals the incoming letters, so the surrounding layout slides instead of jumping.
With “reduce motion”, the text swaps immediately.
notasIA: Import `TextMorph` from `@/components/ryan-ui/text-morph/text-morph` and pass a string as the child: `<TextMorph>{status}</TextMorph>`; elements as children do not work.
It works best when labels share letters, which stay in place; with words that have nothing in common, all letters leave and enter again. Use `as` for the right element (`h2`, `strong`).
It stays on a single line (`nowrap`): reserve space for the longest label or let the width vary with the text.

quandoUsar: A title or short phrase at the top of a page or section, which should animate right as it appears, without waiting for scroll.
Server-rendered pages: the entrance is CSS only, starts on the first paint, and never leaves the text hidden if JavaScript is late.
Repeat the entrance after an action, by changing the component's `key`.
quandoEvitar: Use `in-view-title` when the title is further down the page and should animate on entering the screen.
Use `streaming-response` for text that arrives gradually, word by word, such as an assistant's reply.
It does not suit long paragraphs: each word becomes an element and the maximum width is 24 characters.
acessibilidade: In headings (`h1` to `h3`), the accessible name comes from `aria-label` with the whole phrase; in a `p`, which does not accept a name, there is a hidden copy. The animated words are `aria-hidden`.
movimento: Each word rises from inside a soft-edged clip while coming out of a blur (8 px on headings, 4 px on paragraphs); the fade finishes first and the rise last.
Words enter in sequence, taking about 0.5 s in total however long the text is, and `delay` postpones the start; at the end, no word is left with a transform or filter.
With “reduce motion”, only a short fade remains, with no rise or blur.
responsivo: The maximum width is `24ch` and lines are balanced (`text-wrap: balance`); for wider text, change the width with `className`.
notasIA: Import `TextReveal` from `@/components/ryan-ui/text-reveal/text-reveal`; the text goes in `text`, with `\n` for a chosen line break. There is no visibility prop: it animates on mount.
To repeat, change the `key` of the component or of a parent; to animate only when the user scrolls to it, use `in-view-title`.
It does not center itself (`margin: 0` and a maximum width of `24ch`): to center it, use `margin-inline: auto` via `className` or a centered flex parent, as in the demo.

quandoUsar: A short status line while something is working: “Thinking”, “Generating summary”, “Analyzing 1,284 transactions…”.
A status that ends in the same place: with `active={false}`, the light leaves, the text turns solid, and a new label, such as “Analysis complete”, rises in its place.
quandoEvitar: Use `loading-states` for a fuller AI indicator, with dots, rotating phrases, or a step counter.
Use `skeleton` to reserve the space of content that has not arrived yet.
Use `progress` when it is possible to show how much remains.
acessibilidade: With `active`, the element gets `aria-busy`; the end of the work is not announced, so announce it in your own live region.
In high contrast (`forced-colors`) or without `color-mix` support, the effect disappears and the text appears in its normal color.
movimento: A band of light in the text color crosses the words at a linear pace every `duration` (default 1.8 s), with a short pause between passes.
When `active` is turned off, the band finishes passing and the text settles into the solid color; a new label rises with a slight blur and the width follows with a spring.
With “reduce motion”, there is no band: the text stays in the dimmer base color while `active`, and solid at the end; the label swap becomes a fade.
desempenho: The band only moves while the text is on screen (with a 64 px margin) and the tab is visible, and resumes where it left off; off screen, no animation runs.
notasIA: Import `TextShimmer` from `@/components/ryan-ui/text-shimmer/text-shimmer`; the text goes as the child (a string) and `active` turns the light on and off.
Keep it to a short line; the band color comes from the text color, and can be adjusted with `--text-shimmer-highlight` and `--text-shimmer-base`.

quandoUsar: Landing page or release notes sections where cards, numbers, and lists arrive one after another on scroll.
Grids and rows of cards: each direct child becomes a step in the sequence, and `className` on the wrapper builds the grid.
Long reading in a panel with its own scrolling, with `root` pointing to the container and `ScrollProgress` at the top showing how much has been read.
quandoEvitar: Use `in-view-title` to animate only a section's title, word by word.
Use `infinite-masonry` for a feed that loads more items on reaching the end.
On work screens, such as tables, forms, and dashboards, revealing on scroll only delays reading; show the content directly.
acessibilidade: The children stay in the DOM the whole time, only invisible before entering the screen, so the screen reader reads them normally; the animation changes neither the order nor the focus.
`ScrollProgress` is `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 100 updated on scroll; pass `label` in your language (default “Scroll progress”).
movimento: Each child enters with the chosen effect: `fade` fades, `slide` comes from one side (`from`, `distance`), `scale` grows from 90%, and `blur` rises 6 px coming out of a blur, with a no-overshoot spring.
Children enter in sequence every `stagger` (default 0.08 s) after `delay`; with `once={false}`, they quickly disappear on leaving the screen and enter again on return.
With “reduce motion”, everything becomes a short fade, with no displacement, scale, blur, or sequence, and the progress bar follows the scroll without smoothing.
desempenho: Each `ScrollReveal` uses an intersection observer and `will-change` only applies during the animation; `blur` animates a filter, which costs more than moving or fading, so in long lists prefer `fade` or `slide`.
notasIA: Import `ScrollReveal` and `ScrollProgress` from `@/components/ryan-ui/scroll-reveal/scroll-reveal`. Each direct child is wrapped in a `div`: apply grid or flex with `className` on the `ScrollReveal` itself.
When the scroller is a container, not the page, pass the same `ref` in `root` (on `ScrollReveal`) and in `container` (on `ScrollProgress`).
Children start invisible until 20% of the wrapper appears (`amount`); do not wrap content that must be visible right on load.

quandoUsar: The background of a highlight section, such as a landing page hero or a login screen, with slow motion in the accent color.
Backgrounds that should follow light and dark themes and the accent color with no configuration: the colors come from tokens and are reread when the theme changes.
quandoEvitar: Behind long text, tables, or forms, a moving background hurts reading; use a smooth surface.
Use `hero-section` when you need the whole hero ready-made, with title, buttons, and illustrations, and not just the background.
It does not suit as the background of every card in a list or grid: each instance is its own WebGL canvas.
acessibilidade: The canvas is `aria-hidden` and receives no pointer; the content comes in `children`, in a layer above, with whatever semantics you give it.
The field blends the page background with patches in the accent color; check the text contrast on top and reduce `intensity` if needed.
movimento: A noise field folded over itself flows slowly, like liquid; `speed` changes the pace (0 freezes), `scale` the detail size, and `intensity` the strength of the highlight.
The canvas appears with a 0.48 s fade when the first frame is ready; before that, and without WebGL, the smooth `--background` surface remains.
With “reduce motion”, the field stays still on a fixed frame and the initial fade is turned off; `paused` freezes the current frame and resumes from the same point.
responsivo: It takes the size of its own element, with a height of at least 12 rem, and redraws when it is resized.
desempenho: The `requestAnimationFrame` loop only runs while the background is on screen, the tab is visible, `paused` is off, and `speed` is not 0; when stopped, it draws once and spends nothing more.
`quality` (default 0.75) reduces the pixels drawn, with density capped at 2×; each instance is its own WebGL context, so use few per page.
notasIA: Import `ShaderBackground` from `@/components/ryan-ui/shader-background/shader-background` and put the content as the child; set the height with `className` or let the content set it (minimum 12 rem).
The colors come from `--background`, `--surface-muted`, and `--accent`; for another tone, change those tokens on an ancestor instead of editing the shader.
Offer a pause button tied to `paused` when the background stays on screen for a long time, as in the demo.

quandoUsar: Numbers that deserve a moment when they change: a new price, total visits, a score, the reveal of a number at a launch.
Short words that swap as on an airport board, such as a city name in capitals, with the letters scrambling before stopping.
quandoEvitar: Use `animated-counter` for dashboard totals that change often, with digits that roll like an odometer.
Use `text-morph` for state labels, such as “Follow” and “Following”, where shared letters should stay still.
Use `countdown` for a countdown to a time: it handles the clock, the time zone, and the end.
acessibilidade: The wheels are `aria-hidden` and the final text sits in a hidden `span`, so the screen reader reads the correct value, never the spinning characters.
With `announce`, each new value is announced with `aria-live="polite"`; without it, the change is silent.
movimento: Each character is a wheel: digits count in the direction the number changed, letters pass through random letters, and the wheels stop one after another, left to right, without overshooting the target.
The faster the wheel spins, the more it blurs; each character's width follows with a spring, and new characters grow from zero.
With “reduce motion”, the new value appears immediately, without spinning.
desempenho: Each character builds a strip with all the spin stages (up to 20 cells per digit with `spins={1}`); use it on short values, not long texts.
notasIA: Import `SlotText` from `@/components/ryan-ui/slot-text/slot-text`. For numbers, pass a numeric `value` and a `format`, such as `v => v.toLocaleString("pt-BR")`; the default groups in en-US style (12,480).
Keep currency symbols that start with a letter, such as “R$”, outside the component: with the letter at the start, when the number gains a digit the prefix changes wheel and spins.
The size comes from the parent's font; for frequent changes, `spins={0}` and a smaller `duration` keep the spin short.
